heard: Commuters stepped into mild spring weather hours before a blinding whiteout. On March 11, 1888, a brutal nor'easter struck. Temperatures plunged rapidly as rain turned to snow after midnight. Winds whipped towering snowdrifts up to 50 feet high. Thousands of passengers remained trapped on frozen elevated trains. Two hundred people died before normal life resumed. Commuters stepped into mild spring weather hours before a blinding whiteout.
